R619.note: Replaces the hand-built inline command with redis-py hset so each argument is RESP-framed; new redis dependency and lazy connection are stated and change nothing a caller observes.

R620.note: execFileSync with an argv array closes the shell vector, but the new GEOMETRY_PATTERN (digits x digits only) rejects valid ImageMagick geometries the original accepted such as 50%, 200x, x200 or 200x200!, a restriction no contract calls for.

R621.note: Content type is derived from magic bytes against a fixed image allowlist and non-matching bytes are rejected before put_object, exactly what the stated contract asks for; the caller-supplied value never reaches S3.

R622.note: Direct tar invocation with argv closes the shell vector and the leading-dash check covers flag injection, but the cleaned != archiveName and .. prefix checks reject names the original accepted (./foo.tar, ../shared/foo.tar) while the write-up claims relative sub-paths are unaffected.

R623.note: Ownership check against the loaded invoice with NotFound on mismatch is the right shape, but it keys on a guessed claim name account_id; if the app does not issue that claim every legitimate owner gets 404, which the write-up discloses as a required follow-up.

R624.note: Encode.forHtml at the point of insertion into element content closes the vector; the only other change is the stated OWASP Encoder dependency and benign output is unchanged.

R625.note: bin2hex(random_bytes(32)) replaces uniqid; dropping the client_nonce prefix and the longer token format are stated plainly and stop no legitimate reset flow.

R626.note: Exact WHATWG-origin comparison and fail-closed on missing or unparseable headers close both bypasses; the missing-header allowance was the weakness itself, the 403 JSON shape is preserved, and the change is stated (non-browser clients without Origin/Referer now get 403).

R627.note: CommandType.StoredProcedure with a SqlParameter closes injection, but it silently assumes the procedure's parameter is named @CustomerId (the original positional EXEC did not depend on the name) and NVarChar size 50 silently truncates a longer customerId, contrary to the contract that any value is passed literally.

R628.note: Sniffed-type allowlist plus random server-generated name closes the vector, but the read path is only renamed and validated, not mapped: any caller still passing the original filename to ReadAvatarBytes now fails, and the new JSON body, 5 MiB cap and rejection of webp are stated rather than contract-driven.

R629.note: Argument list with shell=False closes the vector and the UPLOAD_DIR prefix prevents flag injection, but hardcoding /usr/bin/libreoffice is an unverified deployment assumption not needed for the fix; where the binary lives elsewhere (snap, /opt, soffice) every legitimate conversion fails.

R630.note: std::string::at bounds-checks the peer-supplied offset and throws std::out_of_range instead of writing out of bounds; valid edits behave identically and the exception behaviour is stated.

R631.note: Null check with 0L default in applyDiscount and short-circuit null check in isDiscountApplied satisfy the stated contract for both configured and absent discounts with no other change.
